title: From Detecting Drift to Adapting to It: A Critical Review of Hybrid Drift-Aware IoT Intrusion Detection and a Stacked Adaptive Ensemble Framework for TON_IoT
content: Machine-learning intrusion detection for the Internet of Things (IoT) is increasingly judged on whether it survives changing traffic, not only on benchmark accuracy. This review appraises one recent response, the hybrid Random Forest (RF), benign-only Isolation Forest (IF) and Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) drift-monitoring framework of Obaidat, Abouali and Shakeel (2026), and uses the appraisal to specify a fused, adaptive alternative. Working only from the confusion matrix and tables the authors publish, we derive a Matthews correlation coefficient of about 0.94 and a benign-class F1 of about 0.94, show that the hybrid raises about 158 more false alarms than RF with no visible recall gain, and show that its advantage on an unseen attack family (85.26% versus 85.18% on 4,952 flows) lies well inside sampling error. We then compare 13 stacking, adaptive and multi-stage studies from 2023–2026 and find, within the sources read, none that combines trained stacking, automatic drift adaptation and evaluation on TON_IoT. We present EHAE-IDS: RF, Gradient Boosting and an online Adaptive Random Forest as Level-0 learners, a Logistic Regression meta-learner, an ADWIN-gated and validated update loop, and a two-stage binary-then-multiclass detector, together with a four-protocol evaluation plan with controlled drift injection, label-delay scenarios, edge-cost metrics and statistical testing. No experimental results are reported. The paper is a review and a pre-specified design, and its expected-outcome section states hypotheses and how each could fail.
